process\n423\t    /// and returning [`CanaryTestResult::TimedOut`] if it exceeds `test_timeout`.\n424\t    fn run_test(\n425\t        &self,\n426\t        bead_id: &str,\n427\t        expected: &ExpectedOutcome,\n428\t        testing_binary: &Path,\n429\t    ) -> CanaryTestResult {\n430\t        let start = Instant::now();\n431\t        let timeout = Duration::from_secs(self.test_timeout);\n432\t\n433\t        // Spawn the testing binary against the canary workspace.\n434\t        //\n435\t        // `--workspace` alone does NOT confine the worker. The Explore strand is\n436\t        // enabled by default and, with `workspaces` empty, scans\n437\t        // `workspace_root` — which defaults to $HOME — for every bead workspace\n438\t        // on the box. A canary worker spawned without isolation therefore roams\n439\t        // into the operator's real repos and dispatches agents against them: on\n440\t        // 2026-08-07 a single `needle upgrade` put four agents into spaxel and\n441\t        // bead-forge, where they ran git commands and left files behind. This is\n442\t        // the same escape ADR-006 documents for tests, and the isolation policy\n443\t        // in CLAUDE.md was never applied to the canary runner itself.\n444\t        //\n445\t        // Pin the scan root to the canary workspace and switch Explore off, so a\n446\t        // canary run can only ever touch beads that live in the canary.\n447\t        //\n448\t        // CRITICAL: Set NEEDLE_INNER=1 to prevent the worker from detaching into\n449\t        // tmux. Without this, the worker runs in the background and the canary\n450\t        // evaluates outcomes before work finishes, producing false negatives.\n451\t        //\n452\t        // CRITICAL: Isolate HOME to prevent reading global config at\n453\t        // ~/.config/needle/config.yaml or ~/.needle/. This ensures the canary\n454\t        // worker only reads from the canary workspace's .needle.yaml.\n455\t        //\n456\t        // CRITICAL: Use explicit adapter selection (echo) to avoid inheriting\n457\t        // obsolete adapter names from global config (e.g., 'opus' which was\n458\t        // deprecated in favor of 'claude-anthropic-opus'). The echo adapter is\n459\t        // hermetic and always available for testing.\n460\t        //\n461\t        // Use retry wrapper to handle ETXTBSY (errno 26) which can occur when\n462\t        // spawning a testing binary that was written to disk immediately before\n463\t        // execution (race condition between write close and kernel page cache sync).\n464\t        let mut child = match crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential_child(\n465\t            || {\n466\t                Command::new(testing_binary)\n467\t                    .args([\n468\t                        \"run\",\n469\t                        \"--workspace\",\n470\t                        &self.canary_workspace.display().to_string(),\n471\t                        \"--agent\",\n472\t                        \"echo\", // Use explicit hermetic adapter, not global default\n473\t                        \"--identifier\",\n474\t                        &format!(\"canary-{bead_id}\"),\n475\t                        \"--count\",\n476\t                        \"1\",\n477\t                    ])\n478\t                    .env(\"NEEDLE_INNER\", \"1\")\n479\t                    .env(\"NEEDLE_STRANDS__EXPLORE__ENABLED\", \"false\")\n480\t                    .env(\n481\t                        \"NEEDLE_STRANDS__EXPLORE__WORKSPACE_ROOT\",\n482\t                        &self.canary_workspace,\n483\t                    )\n484\t                    .env(\"HOME\", &self.canary_workspace)\n485\t                    .spawn()\n486\t            },\n487\t            10,\n488\t            20,\n489\t        ) {\n490\t            Ok(c) => c,\n491\t            Err(e) => {\n492\t                return CanaryTestResult::Error {\n493\t                    bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n494\t                    message: format!(\"failed to spawn testing binary: {e}\"),\n495\t                };\n496\t            }\n497\t        };\n498\t\n499\t        // Poll for Ok(None) => {\n504\t                    if start.elapsed() >= timeout {\n505\t                        child.kill().ok();\n506\t                        return CanaryTestResult::TimedOut {\n507\t                            bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n508\t                            elapsed_secs: start.elapsed().as_secs(),\n509\t                        };\n510\t                    }\n511\t                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500));\n512\t                }\n513\t                Err(e) => {\n514\t                    return CanaryTestResult::Error {\n515\t                        bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n516\t                        message: format!(\"failed to wait for testing binary: {e}\"),\n517\t                    };\n518\t                }\n519\t            }\n520\t        };\n521\t\n522\t        let actual = match self.get_actual_outcome(bead_id, exit_code) {\n523\t            Ok(a) => a,\n524\t            Err(e) => {\n525\t                return CanaryTestResult::Error {\n526\t                    bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n527\t                    message: format!(\"failed to get actual outcome: {e}\"),\n528\t                };\n529\t            }\n530\t        };\n531\t\n532\t        // Compare actual vs expected.\n533\t        if self.outcomes_match(expected, &actual) {\n534\t            CanaryTestResult::Passed {\n535\t                bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n536\t                expected: expected.clone(),\n537\t                actual,\n538\t            }\n539\t        } else {\n540\t            let reason = self.mismatch_reason(expected, &actual);\n541\t            CanaryTestResult::Failed {\n542\t                bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n543\t                expected: expected.clone(),\n544\t                actual,\n545\t                reason,\n546\t            }\n547\t        }\n548\t    }\n549\t\n550\t    /// Get the actual outcome for a test bead by querying the bead store.\n551\t    fn CanaryTestResult::Passed { .. } => passed += 1,\n                CanaryTestResult::Failed { .. } => failed += 1,\n                CanaryTestResult::TimedOut { .. } => timed_out += 1,\n                CanaryTestResult::Error { .. } => errors += 1,\n            }\n            results.push(result);\n        }\n\n        let suite_passed = failed == 0 && timed_out == 0 && errors == 0;\n        let binding that may not exist in production.\n    fn validate_bead_backend_binding(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let workspace_config = crate::config::ConfigLoader::load_workspace(&self.canary_workspace)\n            .with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"failed to load .needle.yaml for canary workspace {}\",\n                    self.canary_workspace.display()\n                )\n            })?;\n\n        // Both a missing `.needle.yaml` (`load_workspace` yields `None`) and a\n        // missing .as_ref()\n            .and_then(|overrides| overrides.bead_cli.as_ref())\n        {\n            Some(cli) if !matches!(cli.backend, crate::config::BeadBackend::Auto) => cli,\n            _ => killing the process\n    /// and returning [`CanaryTestResult::TimedOut`] if it exceeds `test_timeout`.\n    fn run_test(\n        &self,\n        bead_id: &str,\n        expected: &ExpectedOutcome,\n        testing_binary: &Path,\n    ) -> CanaryTestResult {\n        let start = Instant::now();\n        let timeout = Duration::from_secs(self.test_timeout);\n\n        // Spawn the testing binary against the canary workspace.\n        //\n        // `--workspace` alone does NOT confine the worker. The Explore strand is\n        // enabled by default and, with `workspaces` empty, scans\n        // `workspace_root` — which defaults to $HOME — for every bead workspace\n        // on the box. A canary worker spawned without isolation therefore roams\n        // into the operator's real repos and dispatches agents against them: on\n        // 2026-08-07 a single `needle upgrade` put four agents into spaxel and\n        // bead-forge, where they ran git commands and left files behind. This is\n        // the same escape ADR-006 documents for tests, and the isolation policy\n        // in CLAUDE.md was never applied to the canary runner itself.\n        //\n        // Pin the scan root to the canary workspace and switch Explore off, so a\n        // canary run can only ever touch beads that live in the canary.\n        //\n        // CRITICAL: Set NEEDLE_INNER=1 to prevent the worker from detaching into\n        // tmux. Without this, the worker runs in the background and the canary\n        // evaluates outcomes before work finishes, producing false negatives.\n        //\n        // CRITICAL: Isolate HOME to prevent reading global config at\n        // ~/.config/needle/config.yaml or ~/.needle/. This ensures the canary\n        // worker only reads from the canary workspace's .needle.yaml.\n        //\n        // CRITICAL: Use explicit adapter selection (echo) to avoid inheriting\n        // obsolete adapter names from global config (e.g., 'opus' which was\n        // deprecated in favor of 'claude-anthropic-opus'). The echo adapter is\n        // hermetic and always available for testing.\n        //\n        // Use retry wrapper to handle ETXTBSY (errno 26) which can occur when\n        // spawning a testing binary that was written to disk immediately before\n        // execution (race condition between write close and kernel page cache sync).\n        let mut child = match crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential_child(\n            || {\n                Command::new(testing_binary)\n                    .args([\n                        \"run\",\n                        \"--workspace\",\n                        &self.canary_workspace.display().to_string(),\n                        \"--agent\",\n                        \"echo\", // Use explicit hermetic adapter, not global default\n                        \"--identifier\",\n                        &format!(\"canary-{bead_id}\"),\n                        \"--count\",\n                        \"1\",\n                    ])\n                    .env(\"NEEDLE_INNER\", \"1\")\n                    .env(\"NEEDLE_STRANDS__EXPLORE__ENABLED\", \"false\")\n                    .env(\n                        \"NEEDLE_STRANDS__EXPLORE__WORKSPACE_ROOT\",\n                        &self.canary_workspace,\n                    )\n                    .env(\"HOME\", &self.canary_workspace)\n                    .spawn()\n            },\n            10,\n            20,\n        ) {\n            Ok(c) => c,\n            Err(e) => {\n                return CanaryTestResult::Error {\n                    bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                    message: format!(\"failed to spawn testing binary: {e}\"),\n                };\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Poll for completion, enforcing the timeout.\n        let exit_code = loop {\n            match child.try_wait() {\n                Ok(Some(status)) => break status.code(),\n                Ok(None) => {\n                    if start.elapsed() >= timeout {\n                        child.kill().ok();\n                        return CanaryTestResult::TimedOut {\n                            bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                            elapsed_secs: start.elapsed().as_secs(),\n                        };\n                    }\n                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500));\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    return CanaryTestResult::Error {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                        message: format!(\"failed to wait for testing binary: {e}\"),\n                    };\n                }\n            }\n        };\n\n        let actual = match self.get_actual_outcome(bead_id, exit_code) {\n            Ok(a) => {e}\"),\n                };\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Compare actual vs expected.\n        if self.outcomes_match(expected, &actual) {\n            CanaryTestResult::Passed {\n                bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                expected: expected.clone(),\n                actual,\n            }\n        } else {\n            let reason = self.mismatch_reason(expected, &actual);\n            CanaryTestResult::Failed {\n                bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                expected: expected.clone(),\n                actual,\n                reason,\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get the actual outcome for a test bead by querying the bead store.\n    fn get_actual_outcome(&self, bead_id: &str, exit_code: Option<i32>) -> Result<ActualOutcome> {\n        let workspace_config = crate::config::ConfigLoader::load_workspace(&self.canary_workspace)?\n            .with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"canary workspace {} has no .needle.yaml\",\n                    self.canary_workspace.display()\n                )\n            })?;\n        let bead_cli = workspace_config.bead_cli.with_context(|| {\n       )\n        })?;\n\n        let output = crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync(\n            || {\n                Command::new(&binary)\n                    .args([\"show\", bead_id, .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(|s| s.to_string()))\n                    .collect()\n            })\n            .unwrap_or_default();\n\n        Ok(ActualOutcome {\n            exit_code,\n fn outcomes_match(&self, expected: &ExpectedOutcome, actual: &ActualOutcome) -> bool {\n        match expected {\n            ExpectedOutcome::Success {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                actual.final_status == *final_status\n                    && labels.iter().all(|l| actual.labels.contains(l))\n                    && actual.exit_code == Some(0)\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Failure {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                actual.final_status == *final_status\n                    && labels.iter().all(|l| actual.labels.contains(l))\n                    && actual.exit_code.is_some_and(|c| c != 0)\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Timeout { final_status } *final_status\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::StateMachine { transitions } => {\n                // Check that all expected transitions occurred.\n                transitions\n                    .iter()\n                    .all(|t| actual.state_transitions.contains(t))\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Generate a human-readable reason for mismatch.\n    fn mismatch_reason(&self, expected: &ExpectedOutcome, actual: &ActualOutcome) -> String {\n        match expected {\n            ExpectedOutcome::Success {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                let mut reasons = Vec::new();\n                if actual.final_status != *final_status {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\n                        \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                        final_status, actual.final_status\n                    ));\n                }\n                for label in labels {\n                    if !actual.labels.contains(label) {\n                        reasons.push(format!(\"missing label: '{}'\", label));\n                    }\n                }\n                if actual.exit_code != Some(0) {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\"expected exit 0, got {:?}\", actual.exit_code));\n                }\n                reasons.join(\"; \")\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Failure {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                let mut reasons = Vec::new();\n                if actual.final_status != *final_status {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\n                        \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                        final_status, actual.final_status\n                    ));\n                }\n                for label in labels {\n                    if !actual.labels.contains(label) {\n                        reasons.push(format!(\"missing label: '{}'\", label));\n                    }\n                }\n                if actual.exit_code == Some(0) {\n                    reasons.push(\"expected non-zero exit, got 0\".to_string());\n                }\n                reasons.join(\"; \")\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Timeout { final_status } => {\n                format!(\n                    \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                    final_status, actual.final_status\n                )\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::StateMachine { transitions } => {\n                let missing: Vec<_> = transitions\n                    .iter()\n                    .filter(|t| !actual.state_transitions.contains(*t))\n                    .collect();\n                format!(\"missing state transitions: {:?}\", missing)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Promote :testing to :stable, backing up the current :stable.\n    ///\n    /// This operation is atomic at the filesystem level:\n    /// 1. Move :stable to :stable.prev\n    /// 2. Move :testing to :stable\n    /// 3. Update symlink\n    pub fn promote(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        if !testing.exists() {\n            bail!(\"testing binary not found: {}\", testing.display());\n        }\n\n        // Ensure bin directory exists.\n        let bin_dir = self.needle_home.join(\"bin\");\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&bin_dir).context(\"failed to create bin directory\")?;\n\n        // Step 1: Remove old backup if exists.\n        if prev.exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&prev).context(\"failed to remove old backup\")?;\n        }\n\n        // Step 2: Move current stable to backup (if exists).\n        if stable.exists() {\n            std::fs::rename(&stable, &prev).context(\"failed to backup stable binary\")?;\n        }\n\n        // Step 3: Move testing to stable.\n        std::fs::rename(&testing, &stable).context(\"failed to promote testing to stable\")?;\n\n        // Step 4: Update symlink.\n        if symlink.exists() || symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&symlink).context(\"failed to remove old symlink\")?;\n        }\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to create symlink\")?;\n        #[cfg(not(unix))]\n        {\n            // Fallback: copy instead of symlink on non-Unix.\n            std::fs::copy(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to copy stable to symlink\")?;\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            testing = %testing.display(),\n            stable = %stable.display(),\n            prev = %prev.display(),\n            symlink = %symlink.display(),\n            \"promoted testing to stable\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Reject :testing (discard without promoting).\n    ///\n    /// The fleet remains on :stable unchanged.\n    pub fn reject(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n\n        if testing.exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&testing).context(\"failed to remove testing binary\")?;\n            tracing::info!(path = %testing.display(), \"rejected testing binary\");\n        } else {\n            tracing::warn!(\"no testing binary to reject\");\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Rollback to the previous stable binary.\n    ///\n    /// Restores :stable.prev as :stable.\n    pub fn rollback(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        if !prev.exists() {\n            bail!(\"no previous stable binary to rollback to\");\n        }\n\n        // Move current stable aside (if exists) - it becomes the new backup.\n        if stable.exists() {\n            // Remove the old backup first since we're about to replace it.\n            let old_backup = self.needle_home.join(\"bin/needle-stable.rollback\");\n            if old_backup.exists() {\n                std::fs::remove_file(&old_backup)?;\n            }\n            std::fs::rename(&stable, &old_backup)?;\n        }\n\n        // Restore previous stable.\n        std::fs::rename(&prev, &stable).context(\"failed to restore previous stable\")?;\n\n        // Update symlink.\n        if symlink.exists() || symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&symlink)?;\n        }\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to update symlink\")?;\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            stable = %stable.display(),\n            \"rolled back to previous stable\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Check the current release channel status.\n    pub fn status(&self) -> Result<ChannelStatus> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        let testing_exists = testing.exists();\n        let stable_exists = stable.exists();\n        let prev_exists = prev.exists();\n\n        let symlink_target = if symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::read_link(&symlink).ok()\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n\n        Ok(ChannelStatus {\n            testing_exists,\n            stable_exists,\n            prev_exists,\n            symlink_target,\n            testing_path: `Outcome::classify()`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Outcome {\n    /// Exit 0 — agent completed work successfully.\n    Success,\n    /// Non-zero exit indicating a failure (includes app errors 1-99 and unknown codes).\n    Failure,\n    /// Exit 100 or 124 — timeout wrapper expired.\n    Timeout,\n    /// Exit 126 or 127 — agent binary not found or not executable.\n `was_interrupted` flag takes precedence over exit code analysis.\n    ///\n    /// # Mapping (per spec)\n    /// - `was_interrupted=true` → `Interrupted` (checked first)\n    /// - exit 0 → `Success`\n    /// - exit 1 → `Failure`\n    /// - exit 124 → `Timeout`\n    /// - exit 127 → `AgentNotFound`\n    /// - exit >128 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    /// - exit <0 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    ///   // if a new Outcome variant is added without updating this match.\n        match exit_code {\n            // Success\n            0 => Outcome::Success,\n            // Explicit failure code\n            1 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Timeout (GNU timeout exit code)\n            124 => Outcome::Timeout,\n            // Agent not found (shell exit code for missing command)\n            127 125..=128 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Signal exits: >128 (128 + signal number)\n            // These are all crashes per the spec.\n            129..=i32::MAX => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// DecompositionMode\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Mode distinguishing timeout-driven decomposition from ordinary failure handling.\n///\n/// This enum defines the API boundary between two distinct failure-handling paths:\n/// - **Timeout mode**: Activated when a bead times out. The bead is decomposed\n///   into smaller child beads via `ChildBeadProposal`, each representing a\n///   phase of the original work. This is a recovery strategy for work that\n///   exceeded its time budget but may still be completable in smaller pieces.\n/// - **OrdinaryFailure mode**: Activated for any non-timeout failure (compilation\n///   error, test failure, agent crash, etc.). The bead is NOT decomposed.\n///   It is either retried, released, or escalated based on the failure type\n///   and consecutive failure count.\n///\n/// # When to use each mode\n///\n/// **Use `Timeout` mode when:**\n/// - An agent process exits with code 124 (GNU timeout) or times out via another wrapper\n/// - The bead has made progress but exceeded its time budget\n/// - The work can be meaningfully split into discrete phases\n/// - Child beads can complete the work with the same or reduced timeout\n///\n/// **Use `OrdinaryFailure` mode when:**\n/// - Exit codes 1-123, 125-128 (failure codes) or 127 (agent not found)\n/// - Exit codes >128 (signal crashes)\n/// - Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n/// - The failure is NOT time-related and splitting won't help\n///\n/// # API boundary\n///\n/// This enum is the sole discriminator for whether the decomposition path is\n/// activated. The bead should be retried, released, or escalated\n    /// via the normal failure-handling path.\n    OrdinaryFailure,\n}\n\nimpl DecompositionMode {\n    /// Returns true if this is timeout decomposition mode.\n    ///\n    /// This is the primary query method for routing to the decomposition path.\n    /// All code that needs to know whether to decompose should call this method\n    /// rather than inspecting the enum directly.\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: Some(\"Phase 1\".to_string()),\n    /// };\n    /// assert!(mode.is_timeout());\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert!(!mode.is_timeout());\n    /// ```\n    pub fn is_timeout(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionMode::Timeout { .. })\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if this is ordinary failure mode.\n    ///\n    /// This is the primary query method for routing to the normal failure\n    /// handling path (retry, release, or escalate without decomposition).\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert!(mode.is_ordinary_failure());\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n    /// };\n    /// assert!(!mode.is_ordinary_failure());\n    /// ```\n    pub fn is_ordinary_failure(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the timeout duration if in timeout mode, None otherwise.\n    ///\n    /// This is a convenience method for extracting the timeout value without\n    /// pattern matching. Returns `None` for `OrdinaryFailure` mode.\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n    /// };\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.timeout_seconds(), Some(120));\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.timeout_seconds(), None);\n    /// ```\n    pub fn timeout_seconds(&self) -> Option<u64> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n                timeout_seconds, ..\n            } => Some(*timeout_seconds),\n            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the current phase hint if in timeout mode, None otherwise.\n    ///\n    /// This is a convenience method for extracting the optional phase hint\n    /// without pattern matching. Returns `None` for `OrdinaryFailure` mode\n    /// or when the hint is not set.\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: Some(\"Phase 1\".to_string()),\n    /// };\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.current_phase_hint(), Some(&\"Phase 1\".to_string()));\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n    /// };\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.current_phase_hint(), None);\n    /// ```\n    pub fn current_phase_hint(&self) -> Option<&String> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n                current_phase_hint, ..\n            } => current_phase_hint.as_ref(),\n            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for DecompositionMode {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n                timeout_seconds, ..\n            } => write!(f, \"timeout ({}s)\", timeout_seconds),\n            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => write!(f, \"ordinary_failure\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// StrandError / StrandResult\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Error returned by a strand evaluation.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StrandError {\n    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n    ConfigError(String),\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for StrandError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            StrandError::StoreError(e) => {\n                // Show the full error chain, not just the top-level context.\n                // This surfaces the actual stderr/stdout from bf/br commands.\n                write!(f, \"bead store error: {}\", e)?;\n                // Append any error causes from the chain (the actual bf/br stderr)\n                for cause in e.chain().skip(1) {\n                    write!(f, \"\\n  caused by: {}\", cause)?;\n                }\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            StrandError::ConfigError(s) => write!(f, \"strand configuration error: {}\", s),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for StrandError {\n    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {\n        match self {\n            StrandError::StoreError(e) => Some(e.as_ref()),\n            StrandError::ConfigError(_) => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Result of a strand evaluation in the waterfall.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StrandResult {\n    /// One or more candidate beads were found.\n    BeadFound(Vec<Bead>),\n    /// The strand synthesized new work (e.g., mitosis created child beads).\n    WorkCreated,\n    /// This strand found nothing; continue to the next strand.\n    NoWork,\n    /// The strand encountered an error during evaluation.\n    Error(StrandError),\n    /// The strand was skipped because its prerequisites are not met.\n    ///\n    /// This is distinct from `NoWork` (which means \"ran and found nothing\")\n    /// and `Error` (which means \"ran but failed\"). `Skipped` means \"did not\n    /// run because the environment doesn't support it\" — e.g., a strand that\n    /// requires a home bead store when the worker is configured without one.\n    Skipped { reason: String },\n    /// A bead with too many consecutive failures should be split.\n    ///\n    /// Contains the bead to split and the current failure count.\n    Split(Box<Bead>, u32),\n    /// Candidates were found but all were excluded/assigned — short retry needed.\n    ///\n    /// This is distinct from `NoWork` (which means \"truly no candidates\").\n    /// `FoundButExcluded` means \"candidates exist but this worker can't claim\n    /// them right now\" — they're assigned to other workers or blocked by labels.\n    /// This signals the worker to use short retry backoff instead of long idle.\n    FoundButExcluded,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ClaimResult / ClaimOutcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Result of a single claim attempt for one bead.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum ClaimResult {\n    /// This worker successfully claimed the bead.\n    Claimed(Bead),\n    /// Another worker claimed the bead first.\n    RaceLost {\n        /// Assignee that won the race.\n        claimed_by: String,\n    },\n    /// The bead cannot be claimed (not open, blocked, etc.).\n    NotClaimable {\n        /// Human-readable reason.\n        reason: String,\n    },\n    /// Claim CLI failed with a store/CLI error (distinct from race-lost).\n    ClaimError {\n        /// Human-readable error message.\n        reason: String,\n    },\n    /// A claim error threshold was reached — bead/store is suspect.\n    ///\n    /// This variant is emitted when a bead has failed claim attempts N times\n    /// with errors (not race-lost conditions). The bead should be skipped and\n    /// marked as suspect rather than silently cycling.\n    Suspect {\n        /// The bead ID that hit the error threshold.\n        bead_id: BeadId,\n        /// The number of consecutive claim errors.\n        consecutive_errors: u32,\n        /// The most recent error message.\n        last_error: String,\n    },\n}\n\n/// Aggregate outcome after exhausting all candidates for a selection cycle.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\n#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]\npub enum ClaimOutcome {\n    /// Successfully claimed a bead.\n    Claimed(Bead),\n    /// Raced every candidate and lost every time.\n    AllRaceLost,\n    /// The strand returned no candidates.\n    NoCandidates,\n    /// The bead store returned an error.\n    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n    /// A claim error threshold was reached — bead/store is suspect.\n    ///\n    /// This variant is emitted when a bead has failed claim attempts N times\n    /// with errors (not race-lost conditions). The bead should be skipped and\n    /// marked as suspect rather than silently cycling.\n    Suspect {\n        /// The bead ID that hit the error threshold.\n        bead_id: BeadId,\n        /// The number of consecutive claim errors.\n        consecutive_errors: u32,\n        /// The most recent error message.\n        last_error: String,\n    },\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// BrDependency\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A bead dependency as returned from the `br`/`bf` JSON output, or from\n/// bead-rs's `bead` (`{\"blocker\": \"<id>\", \"kind\": \"blocks\"}` — a lean\n/// edge-only shape with no enriched title/status/priority). The aliases\n/// below accept both without changing how bf/br JSON deserializes.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct BrDependency {\n    #[serde(alias = \"blocker\")]\n    pub id: BeadId,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub title: String,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub status: String,\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub priority: Priority,\n    #[serde(rename = \"dependency_type\", alias = \"kind\", default)]\n    pub dependency_type: String,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Bead struct\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Serde helper: treats an empty JSON string as `None`.\nfn empty_string_as_none<'de, D>(d: D) -> Result<Option<String>, D::Error>\nwhere\n    D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,\n{\n    let s = Option::<String>::deserialize(d)?;\n    Ok(s.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()))\n}\n\n/// A comment on a bead.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Comment {\n    /// Comment ID (internal database ID).\n    pub id: i64,\n    /// The bead this comment is on.\n    #[serde(rename = pub created_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n}\n\n/// A bead as returned from the bead store.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct Bead {\n    pub id: BeadId,\n    pub title: String,\n to now so explore can deserialize it\n    #[serde(default = \"chrono::Utc::now\")]\n    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// AgentOutcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Raw output from an agent process (before outcome classification).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct AgentOutcome {\n    pub exit_code: i32,\n    pub stdout: String,\n    pub stderr: String,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// NeedleError\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Top-level NEEDLE error type.\n///\n/// Tier is encoded in the variant, so recovery routing is type-driven.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum NeedleError {\n    /// Transient: retry after backoff (network hiccup, lock contention).\n    Transient {\n        message: String,\n        bead_id: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Bead-scoped: abandon this bead; other beads can proceed.\n    BeadScoped { message: String, bead_id: BeadId },\n    /// Worker-scoped: this worker should shut down; fleet continues.\n    WorkerScoped {\n        message: String,\n        worker_id: WorkerId,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for NeedleError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: Some(id),\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error (bead {}): {}\", id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: None,\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error: {}\", message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::BeadScoped { message, bead_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"bead-scoped error (bead {}): {}\", bead_id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::WorkerScoped { message, worker_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"worker-scoped error (worker {}): {}\", worker_id, message)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for NeedleError {}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(-1, false), Outcome::Crash(-1));\n        assert_eq!(Outcome::classify(-9, false), Outcome::Crash(-9));\n        // Large positive values >255 -> Crash per spec (exit >    // Verify testing binary exists.\n        if !testing_binary.exists() {\n            bail!(\"testing binary not found: {}\", testing_binary.display());\n        }\n\n        // Verify canary workspace exists.\n        if !self.canary_workspace.exists() {\n            bail!(\n                \"canary workspace not found: {}\",\n                self.canary_workspace.display()\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Validate canary workspace has authoritative bead_cli.backend binding.\n        // This prevents the canary from inheriting a machine-local legacy binding\n        // that may not exist in production environments (2026-08-15 incident).\n        self.validate_bead_backend_binding()?;\n\n        // Discover test beads in the canary workspace.\n        let test_beads = self.discover_test_beads()?;\n        if test_beads.is_empty() {\n            bail!(\"no test beads found in canary workspace\");\n        }\n\n        let mut results = Vec::new();\n        let mut passed = 0;\n        let mut failed = 0;\n        let mut timed_out = 0;\n        let mut errors = 0;\n\n        for bead_id in &test_beads {\n            // Load expected outcome for this test.\n            let expected = match self.load_expected_outcome(bead_id) {\n                Ok(e) => e,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    results.push(CanaryTestResult::Error {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        message: format!(\"failed to load expected outcome: {e}\"),\n                    });\n                    errors += 1;\n                    continue;\n                }\n            };\n\n            // Run the test.\n            let result = self.run_test(bead_id, &expected, &testing_binary);\n            match &result {\n                CanaryTestResult::Passed { .. } => passed += 1,\n                CanaryTestResult::Failed { .. } => failed += 1,\n                CanaryTestResult::TimedOut { .. } => timed_out += 1,\n                CanaryTestResult::Error { .. } => errors += 1,\n            }\n            results.push(result);\n        }\n\n        let suite_passed = failed == 0 && timed_out == 0 && errors == 0;\n        let total_tests = test_beads.len();\n\n        Ok(CanaryReport {\n            testing_binary,\n            workspace: self.canary_workspace.clone(),\n            total_tests,\n            passed,\n            failed,\n            timed_out,\n            errors,\n            duration_secs: start.elapsed().as_secs(),\n            results,\n            suite_passed,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Validate that the canary workspace has an authoritative bead_cli.backend binding.\n    ///\n    /// This prevents environmental failures where the canary workspace inherits\n    /// a machine-local legacy binding that may not exist in production.\n    fn validate_bead_backend_binding(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let workspace_config = crate::config::ConfigLoader::load_workspace(&self.canary_workspace)\n            .with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"failed to load .needle.yaml for canary workspace {}\",\n                    self.canary_workspace.display()\n                )\n            })?;\n\n        // Both a missing `.needle.yaml` (`load_workspace` yields `None`) and a\n        // missing `bead_cli` section leave the canary on the same implicit\n        // `auto` binding as an explicit one, so all three are rejected here.\n        let bead_cli = match workspace_config\n            .as_ref()\n            .and_then(|overrides| overrides.bead_cli.as_ref())\n        {\n            Some(cli) if !matches!(cli.backend, crate::config::BeadBackend::Auto) => cli,\n            _ => bail!(\n                \"canary workspace {} has no authoritative bead_cli.backend binding (currently set to 'auto'). \\\n                 This causes environmental failures when the canary inherits a machine-local legacy binding. \\\n                 Fix by adding to {}/.needle.yaml:\\n  bead_cli:\\n    backend: bead-rs\\nor\\n    backend: bead-forge\",\n                self.canary_workspace.display(),\n                self.canary_workspace.display()\n            ),\n        };\n        let backend = &bead_cli.backend;\n\n        // Verify the backend binary exists\n        let (backend_type, binary_path) =\n            crate::config::resolve_bead_cli(bead_cli).with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"failed to resolve bead CLI backend '{}' for canary workspace {}\",\n                    backend,\n                    self.canary_workspace.display()\n                )\n            })?;\n\n        if !binary_path.exists() {\n            bail!(\n                \"bead CLI backend '{}' binary not found: {} (backend: {})\\n\\\n                 Ensure the backend is installed and accessible, or update bead_cli.path in {}/.needle.yaml\",\n                backend,\n                binary_path.display(),\n                backend_type,\n                self.canary_workspace.display()\n            );\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            backend = %backend,\n            binary = %binary_path.display(),\n            resolved_backend = %backend_type,\n            \"canary workspace bead backend validated\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Discover test bead IDs in the canary workspace.\n    fn discover_test_beads(&self) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n        let expected_dir = self.canary_workspace.join(\"expected\");\n        if !expected_dir.exists() {\n            bail!(\n                \"expected outcomes directory not found: {}\",\n                expected_dir.display()\n            );\n        }\n\n        let mut bead_ids = Vec::new();\n        for entry in std::fs::read_dir(&expected_dir)? {\n            let entry = entry?;\n            let path = entry.path();\n            if path.extension().is_some_and(|e| e == \"yaml\") {\n                if let Some(stem) = path.file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) {\n                    bead_ids.push(stem.to_string());\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(bead_ids)\n    }\n\n    /// Load the expected outcome for a test bead.\n    fn load_expected_outcome(&self, bead_id: &str) -> Result<ExpectedOutcome> {\n        let path = self\n            .canary_workspace\n            .join(\"expected\")\n            .join(format!(\"{bead_id}.yaml\"));\n        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read expected outcome: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        serde_yaml::from_str(&content)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid expected outcome YAML: {}\", path.display()))\n    }\n\n    /// Run a single canary test.\n    ///\n    /// Spawns the testing binary and polls for completion, killing the process\n    /// and returning [`CanaryTestResult::TimedOut`] if it exceeds `test_timeout`.\n    fn run_test(\n        &self,\n        bead_id: &str,\n        expected: &ExpectedOutcome,\n        testing_binary: &Path,\n    ) -> CanaryTestResult {\n        let start = Instant::now();\n        let timeout = Duration::from_secs(self.test_timeout);\n\n        // Spawn the testing binary against the canary workspace.\n        //\n        // `--workspace` alone does NOT confine the worker. The Explore strand is\n        // enabled by default and, with `workspaces` empty, scans\n        // `workspace_root` — which defaults to $HOME — for every bead workspace\n        // on the box. A canary worker spawned without isolation therefore roams\n        // into the operator's real repos and dispatches agents against them: on\n        // 2026-08-07 a single `needle upgrade` put four agents into spaxel and\n        // bead-forge, where they ran git commands and left files behind. This is\n        // the same escape ADR-006 documents for tests, and the isolation policy\n        // in CLAUDE.md was never applied to the canary runner itself.\n        //\n        // Pin the scan root to the canary workspace and switch Explore off, so a\n        // canary run can only ever touch beads that live in the canary.\n        //\n        // CRITICAL: Set NEEDLE_INNER=1 to prevent the worker from detaching into\n        // tmux. Without this, the worker runs in the background and the canary\n        // evaluates outcomes before work finishes, producing false negatives.\n        //\n        // CRITICAL: Isolate HOME to prevent reading global config at\n        // ~/.config/needle/config.yaml or ~/.needle/. This ensures the canary\n        // worker only reads from the canary workspace's .needle.yaml.\n        //\n        // CRITICAL: Use explicit adapter selection (echo) to avoid inheriting\n        // obsolete adapter names from global config (e.g., 'opus' which was\n        // deprecated in favor of 'claude-anthropic-opus'). The echo adapter is\n        // hermetic and always available for testing.\n        //\n        // Use retry wrapper to handle ETXTBSY (errno 26) which can occur when\n        // spawning a testing binary that was written to disk immediately before\n        // execution (race condition between write close and kernel page cache sync).\n        let mut child = match crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential_child(\n            || {\n                Command::new(testing_binary)\n                    .args([\n                        \"run\",\n                        \"--workspace\",\n                        &self.canary_workspace.display().to_string(),\n                        \"--agent\",\n                        \"echo\", // Use explicit hermetic adapter, not global default\n                        \"--identifier\",\n                        &format!(\"canary-{bead_id}\"),\n                        \"--count\",\n                        \"1\",\n                    ])\n                    .env(\"NEEDLE_INNER\", \"1\")\n                    .env(\"NEEDLE_STRANDS__EXPLORE__ENABLED\", \"false\")\n                    .env(\n                        \"NEEDLE_STRANDS__EXPLORE__WORKSPACE_ROOT\",\n                        &self.canary_workspace,\n                    )\n                    .env(\"HOME\", &self.canary_workspace)\n                    .spawn()\n            },\n            10,\n            20,\n        ) {\n            Ok(c) => c,\n            Err(e) => {\n                return CanaryTestResult::Error {\n                    bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                    message: format!(\"failed to spawn testing binary: {e}\"),\n                };\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Poll for completion, enforcing the timeout.\n        let exit_code = loop {\n            match child.try_wait() {\n                Ok(Some(status)) => break status.code(),\n                Ok(None) => {\n                    if start.elapsed() >= timeout {\n                        child.kill().ok();\n                        return CanaryTestResult::TimedOut {\n                            bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                            elapsed_secs: start.elapsed().as_secs(),\n                        };\n                    }\n                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500));\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    return CanaryTestResult::Error {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                        message: format!(\"failed to wait for testing binary: {e}\"),\n                    };\n                }\n            }\n        };\n\n        let actual = match self.get_actual_outcome(bead_id, exit_code) {\n            Ok(a) => a,\n            Err(e) => {\n                return CanaryTestResult::Error {\n                    bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                    message: format!(\"failed to get actual outcome: {e}\"),\n                };\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Compare actual vs expected.\n        if self.outcomes_match(expected, &actual) {\n            CanaryTestResult::Passed {\n                bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                expected: expected.clone(),\n                actual,\n            }\n        } else {\n            let reason = self.mismatch_reason(expected, &actual);\n            CanaryTestResult::Failed {\n                bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                expected: expected.clone(),\n                actual,\n                reason,\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get the actual outcome for a test bead by querying the bead store.\n    fn get_actual_outcome(&self, bead_id: &str, exit_code: Option<i32>) -> Result<ActualOutcome> {\n        let workspace_config = crate::config::ConfigLoader::load_workspace(&self.canary_workspace)?\n            .with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"canary workspace {} has no .needle.yaml\",\n                    self.canary_workspace.display()\n                )\n            })?;\n        let bead_cli = workspace_config.bead_cli.with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"canary workspace {} has no authoritative bead_cli.backend binding\",\n                self.canary_workspace.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n        let (_, binary) = crate::config::resolve_bead_cli(&bead_cli).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to resolve canary workspace bead backend '{}'\",\n                bead_cli.backend\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        let output = crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync(\n            || {\n                Command::new(&binary)\n                    .args([\"show\", bead_id, \"--json\"])\n                    .current_dir(&self.canary_workspace)\n                    .output()\n            },\n            5,\n            20,\n        )\n        .with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to run {} show for backend '{}'\",\n                binary.display(),\n                bead_cli.backend\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        if !output.status.success() {\n            bail!(\n                \"backend '{}' show failed for bead {}: {}\",\n                bead_cli.backend,\n                bead_id,\n                String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim()\n            );\n        }\n\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n        let projection: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&stdout)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to parse '{}' show output\", bead_cli.backend))?;\n        // bead-rs returns a one-element array; bead-forge returns an object.\n        let bead = projection\n            .as_array()\n            .and_then(|items| items.first())\n            .unwrap_or(&projection);\n\n        let final_status = bead[\"status\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"unknown\").to_string();\n        let labels = bead[\"labels\"]\n            .as_array()\n            .map(|arr| {\n                arr.iter()\n                    .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(|s| s.to_string()))\n                    .collect()\n            })\n            .unwrap_or_default();\n\n        Ok(ActualOutcome {\n            exit_code,\n            final_status,\n            labels,\n            state_transitions: Vec::new(), // Not tracked in basic canary tests\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Check if actual outcome matches expected outcome.\n    fn outcomes_match(&self, expected: &ExpectedOutcome, actual: &ActualOutcome) -> bool {\n        match expected {\n            ExpectedOutcome::Success {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                actual.final_status == *final_status\n                    && labels.iter().all(|l| actual.labels.contains(l))\n                    && actual.exit_code == Some(0)\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Failure {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                actual.final_status == *final_status\n                    && labels.iter().all(|l| actual.labels.contains(l))\n                    && actual.exit_code.is_some_and(|c| c != 0)\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Timeout { final_status } => {\n                // Timeout is harder to detect from exit code alone.\n                // We check that the bead was not closed (still open/in_progress).\n                actual.final_status == *final_status\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::StateMachine { transitions } => {\n                // Check that all expected transitions occurred.\n                transitions\n                    .iter()\n                    .all(|t| actual.state_transitions.contains(t))\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Generate a human-readable reason for mismatch.\n    fn mismatch_reason(&self, expected: &ExpectedOutcome, actual: &ActualOutcome) -> String {\n        match expected {\n            ExpectedOutcome::Success {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                let mut reasons = Vec::new();\n                if actual.final_status != *final_status {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\n                        \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                        final_status, actual.final_status\n                    ));\n                }\n                for label in labels {\n                    if !actual.labels.contains(label) {\n                        reasons.push(format!(\"missing label: '{}'\", label));\n                    }\n                }\n                if actual.exit_code != Some(0) {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\"expected exit 0, got {:?}\", actual.exit_code));\n                }\n                reasons.join(\"; \")\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Failure {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                let mut reasons = Vec::new();\n                if actual.final_status != *final_status {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\n                        \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                        final_status, actual.final_status\n                    ));\n                }\n                for label in labels {\n                    if !actual.labels.contains(label) {\n                        reasons.push(format!(\"missing label: '{}'\", label));\n                    }\n                }\n                if actual.exit_code == Some(0) {\n                    reasons.push(\"expected non-zero exit, got 0\".to_string());\n                }\n                reasons.join(\"; \")\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Timeout { final_status } => {\n                format!(\n                    \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                    final_status, actual.final_status\n                )\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::StateMachine { transitions } => {\n                let missing: Vec<_> = transitions\n                    .iter()\n                    .filter(|t| !actual.state_transitions.contains(*t))\n                    .collect();\n                format!(\"missing state transitions: {:?}\", missing)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Promote :testing to :stable, backing up the current :stable.\n    ///\n    /// This operation is atomic at the filesystem level:\n    /// 1. Move :stable to :stable.prev\n    /// 2. Move :testing to :stable\n    /// 3. Update symlink\n    pub fn promote(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        if !testing.exists() {\n            bail!(\"testing binary not found: {}\", testing.display());\n        }\n\n        // Ensure bin directory exists.\n        let bin_dir = self.needle_home.join(\"bin\");\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&bin_dir).context(\"failed to create bin directory\")?;\n\n        // Step 1: Remove old backup if exists.\n        if prev.exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&prev).context(\"failed to remove old backup\")?;\n        }\n\n        // Step 2: Move current stable to backup (if exists).\n        if stable.exists() {\n            std::fs::rename(&stable, &prev).context(\"failed to backup stable binary\")?;\n        }\n\n        // Step 3: Move testing to stable.\n        std::fs::rename(&testing, &stable).context(\"failed to promote testing to stable\")?;\n\n        // Step 4: Update symlink.\n        if symlink.exists() || symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&symlink).context(\"failed to remove old symlink\")?;\n        }\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to create symlink\")?;\n        #[cfg(not(unix))]\n        {\n            // Fallback: copy instead of symlink on non-Unix.\n            std::fs::copy(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to copy stable to symlink\")?;\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            testing = %testing.display(),\n            stable = %stable.display(),\n            prev = %prev.display(),\n            symlink = %symlink.display(),\n            \"promoted testing to stable\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Reject :testing (discard without promoting).\n    ///\n    /// The fleet remains on :stable unchanged.\n    pub fn reject(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n\n        if testing.exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&testing).context(\"failed to remove testing binary\")?;\n            tracing::info!(path = %testing.display(), \"rejected testing binary\");\n        } else {\n            tracing::warn!(\"no testing binary to reject\");\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Rollback to the previous stable binary.\n    ///\n    /// Restores :stable.prev as :stable.\n    pub fn rollback(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        if !prev.exists() {\n            bail!(\"no previous stable binary to rollback to\");\n        }\n\n        // Move current stable aside (if exists) - it becomes the new backup.\n        if stable.exists() {\n            // Remove the old backup first since we're about to replace it.\n            let old_backup = self.needle_home.join(\"bin/needle-stable.rollback\");\n            if old_backup.exists() {\n                std::fs::remove_file(&old_backup)?;\n            }\n            std::fs::rename(&stable, &old_backup)?;\n        }\n\n        // Restore previous stable.\n        std::fs::rename(&prev, &stable).context(\"failed to restore previous stable\")?;\n\n        // Update symlink.\n        if symlink.exists() || symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&symlink)?;\n        }\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to update symlink\")?;\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            stable = %stable.display(),\n            \"rolled back to previous stable\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Check the current release channel status.\n    pub fn status(&self) -> Result<ChannelStatus> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        let testing_exists = testing.exists();\n        let stable_exists = stable.exists();\n        let prev_exists = prev.exists();\n\n        let symlink_target = if symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::read_link(&symlink).ok()\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n\n        Ok(ChannelStatus {\n            testing_exists,\n            stable_exists,\n            prev_exists,\n            symlink_target,\n            testing_path: testing,\n            stable_path: stable,\n            prev_path: prev,\n            symlink_path: symlink,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n// release channels.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ChannelStatus {\n    /// Whether :testing binary exists.\n    pub testing_exists: bool,\n    /// Whether :stable binary exists.\n    pub
