against the canary workspace.\n        //\n        // `--workspace` alone does NOT confine the worker. The Explore strand is\n        // enabled by default and, with `workspaces` empty, scans\n        // `workspace_root` — which defaults to $HOME — for every bead workspace\n        // on the box. A canary worker spawned without isolation therefore roams\n        // into the operator's real repos and dispatches agents against them: on\n        // 2026-08-07 a single `needle upgrade` put four agents into spaxel and\n        // bead-forge, where they ran git commands and left files behind. This is\n        // the same escape ADR-006 documents for tests, and the isolation policy\n        // in CLAUDE.md was never applied to the canary runner itself.\n        //\n        // Pin the scan root to the canary workspace and switch Explore off, so a\n        // canary run can only ever touch beads that live in the canary.\n        //\n        // CRITICAL: Set NEEDLE_INNER=1 to prevent the worker from detaching into\n        // tmux. Without this, the worker runs in the background and the canary\n        // evaluates outcomes before work finishes, producing false negatives.\n        //\n        // CRITICAL: Isolate HOME to prevent reading global config at\n        // ~/.config/needle/config.yaml or ~/.needle/. This ensures the canary\n        // worker only reads from the canary workspace's .needle.yaml.\n        //\n        // CRITICAL: Use explicit adapter selection (echo) to avoid inheriting\n        // obsolete adapter names from global config (e.g., 'opus' which was\n        // deprecated in favor of 'claude-anthropic-opus'). The echo adapter is\n        // hermetic and always available for testing.\n        //\n        // Use retry wrapper to handle ETXTBSY (errno 26) which can occur when\n        // spawning a testing binary that was written to disk immediately before\n        // execution (race condition between write close and kernel page cache sync).\n        let mut child = match crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential_child(\n            || {\n                Command::new(testing_binary)\n                    .args([\n                        \"run\",\n                        \"--workspace\",\n                        &self.canary_workspace.display().to_string(),\n                        \"--agent\",\n                        \"echo\", // Use explicit hermetic adapter, not global default\n                        \"--identifier\",\n                        &format!(\"canary-{bead_id}\"),\n                        \"--count\",\n                        \"1\",\n                    ])\n                    .env(\"NEEDLE_INNER\", \"1\")\n                    .env(\"NEEDLE_STRANDS__EXPLORE__ENABLED\", \"false\")\n                    .env(\n                        \"NEEDLE_STRANDS__EXPLORE__WORKSPACE_ROOT\",\n                        &self.canary_workspace,\n                    )\n                    .env(\"HOME\", &self.canary_workspace)\n                    .spawn()\n            },\n            10,\n            20,\n        ) {\n            Ok(c) => c,\n            Err(e) => {\n                return CanaryTestResult::Error {\n                    bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                    message: format!(\"failed to spawn testing binary: {e}\"),\n                };\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Poll for completion, enforcing the timeout.\n        let exit_code = loop {\n            match child.try_wait() {\n                Ok(Some(status)) => break status.code(),\n                Ok(None) => {\n                    if start.elapsed() >= timeout {\n                        child.kill().ok();\n                        return CanaryTestResult::TimedOut {\n                            bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                            elapsed_secs: start.elapsed().as_secs(),\n                        };\n                    }\n                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500));\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    return CanaryTestResult::Error {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                        message: format!(\"failed to wait for testing binary: {e}\"),\n                    };\n                }\n            }\n        };\n\n        let actual = match self.get_actual_outcome(bead_id, exit_code) {\n            Ok(a) => a,\n            Err(e) => {\n                return CanaryTestResult::Error {\n                    bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                    message: format!(\"failed to get actual outcome: {e}\"),\n                };\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Compare actual vs expected.\n        if self.outcomes_match(expected, &actual) {\n            CanaryTestResult::Passed {\n                bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                expected: expected.clone(),\n                actual,\n            }\n        } else {\n            let reason = self.mismatch_reason(expected, &actual);\n            CanaryTestResult::Failed {\n                bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                expected: expected.clone(),\n                actual,\n                reason,\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get the actual outcome for a test bead by querying the bead store.\n    fn get_actual_outcome(&self, bead_id: &str, exit_code: Option<i32>) -> Result<ActualOutcome> {\n        let workspace_config = crate::config::ConfigLoader::load_workspace(&self.canary_workspace)?\n            .with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"canary workspace {} has no .needle.yaml\",\n                    self.canary_workspace.display()\n                )\n            })?;\n        let bead_cli = workspace_config.bead_cli.with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"canary workspace {} has no authoritative bead_cli.backend binding\",\n                self.canary_workspace.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n        let (_, binary) = crate::config::resolve_bead_cli(&bead_cli).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to resolve canary workspace bead backend '{}'\",\n                bead_cli.backend\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        let output = crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync(\n            || {\n                Command::new(&binary)\n                    .args([\"show\", bead_id, \"--json\"])\n                    .current_dir(&self.canary_workspace)\n                    .output()\n            },\n            5,\n            20,\n        )\n        .with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to run {} show for backend '{}'\",\n                binary.display(),\n                bead_cli.backend\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        if !output.status.success() {\n            bail!(\n                \"backend '{}' show failed for bead {}: {}\",\n                bead_cli.backend,\n                bead_id,\n                String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim()\n            );\n        }\n\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n        let projection: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&stdout)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to parse '{}' show output\", bead_cli.backend))?;\n        // bead-rs returns a one-element array; bead-forge returns an object.\n        let bead = projection\n            .as_array()\n            .and_then(|items| items.first())\n            .unwrap_or(&projection);\n\n        let final_status = bead[\"status\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"unknown\").to_string();\n        let labels = bead[\"labels\"]\n            .as_array()\n            .map(|arr| {\n                arr.iter()\n                    .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(|s| s.to_string()))\n                    .collect()\n            })\n            .unwrap_or_default();\n\n        Ok(ActualOutcome {\n            exit_code,\n            final_status,\n            labels,\n            state_transitions: Vec::new(), // Not tracked in basic canary tests\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Check if actual outcome matches expected outcome.\n    fn outcomes_match(&self, expected: &ExpectedOutcome, actual: &ActualOutcome) -> bool {\n        match expected {\n            ExpectedOutcome::Success {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                actual.final_status == *final_status\n                    && labels.iter().all(|l| actual.labels.contains(l))\n                    && actual.exit_code == Some(0)\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Failure {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                actual.final_status == *final_status\n                    && labels.iter().all(|l| actual.labels.contains(l))\n                    && actual.exit_code.is_some_and(|c| c != 0)\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Timeout { final_status } => {\n                // Timeout is harder to detect from exit code alone.\n                // We check that the bead was not closed (still open/in_progress).\n                actual.final_status == *final_status\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::StateMachine { transitions } => {\n                // Check that all expected transitions occurred.\n                transitions\n                    .iter()\n                    .all(|t| actual.state_transitions.contains(t))\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Generate a human-readable reason for mismatch.\n    fn mismatch_reason(&self, expected: &ExpectedOutcome, actual: &ActualOutcome) -> String {\n        match expected {\n            ExpectedOutcome::Success {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                let mut reasons = Vec::new();\n                if actual.final_status != *final_status {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\n                        \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                        final_status, actual.final_status\n                    ));\n                }\n                for label in labels {\n                    if !actual.labels.contains(label) {\n                        reasons.push(format!(\"missing label: '{}'\", label));\n                    }\n                }\n                if actual.exit_code != Some(0) {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\"expected exit 0, got {:?}\", actual.exit_code));\n                }\n                reasons.join(\"; \")\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Failure {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                let mut reasons = Vec::new();\n                if actual.final_status != *final_status {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\n                        \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                        final_status, actual.final_status\n                    ));\n                }\n                for label in labels {\n                    if !actual.labels.contains(label) {\n                        reasons.push(format!(\"missing label: '{}'\", label));\n                    }\n                }\n                if actual.exit_code == Some(0) {\n                    reasons.push(\"expected non-zero exit, got 0\".to_string());\n                }\n                reasons.join(\"; \")\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Timeout { final_status } => {\n                format!(\n                    \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                    final_status, actual.final_status\n                )\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::StateMachine { transitions } => {\n                let missing: Vec<_> = transitions\n                    .iter()\n                    .filter(|t| !actual.state_transitions.contains(*t))\n                    .collect();\n                format!(\"missing state transitions: {:?}\", missing)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Promote :testing to :stable, backing up the current :stable.\n    ///\n    /// This operation is atomic at the filesystem level:\n    /// 1. Move :stable to :stable.prev\n    /// 2. Move :testing to :stable\n    /// 3. Update symlink\n    pub fn promote(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        if !testing.exists() {\n            bail!(\"testing binary not found: {}\", testing.display());\n        }\n\n        // Ensure bin directory exists.\n        let bin_dir = self.needle_home.join(\"bin\");\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&bin_dir).context(\"failed to create bin directory\")?;\n\n        // Step 1: Remove old backup if exists.\n        if prev.exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&prev).context(\"failed to remove old backup\")?;\n        }\n\n        // Step 2: Move current stable to backup (if exists).\n        if stable.exists() {\n            std::fs::rename(&stable, &prev).context(\"failed to backup stable binary\")?;\n        }\n\n        // Step 3: Move testing to stable.\n        std::fs::rename(&testing, &stable).context(\"failed to promote testing to stable\")?;\n\n        // Step 4: Update symlink.\n        if symlink.exists() || symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&symlink).context(\"failed to remove old symlink\")?;\n        }\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to create symlink\")?;\n        #[cfg(not(unix))]\n        {\n            // Fallback: copy instead of symlink on non-Unix.\n            std::fs::copy(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to copy stable to symlink\")?;\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            testing = %testing.display(),\n            stable = %stable.display(),\n            prev = %prev.display(),\n            symlink = %symlink.display(),\n            \"promoted testing to stable\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Reject :testing (discard without promoting).\n    ///\n    /// The fleet remains on :stable unchanged.\n    pub fn reject(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n\n        if testing.exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&testing).context(\"failed to remove testing binary\")?;\n            tracing::info!(path = %testing.display(), \"rejected testing binary\");\n        } else {\n            tracing::warn!(\"no testing binary to reject\");\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Rollback to the previous stable binary.\n    ///\n    /// Restores :stable.prev as :stable.\n    pub fn rollback(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        if !prev.exists() {\n            bail!(\"no previous stable binary to rollback to\");\n        }\n\n        // Move current stable aside (if exists) - it becomes the new backup.\n        if stable.exists() {\n            // Remove the old backup first since we're about to replace it.\n            let old_backup = self.needle_home.join(\"bin/needle-stable.rollback\");\n            if old_backup.exists() {\n                std::fs::remove_file(&old_backup)?;\n            }\n            std::fs::rename(&stable, &old_backup)?;\n        }\n\n        // Restore previous stable.\n        std::fs::rename(&prev, &stable).context(\"failed to restore previous stable\")?;\n\n        // Update symlink.\n        if symlink.exists() || symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&symlink)?;\n        }\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to update symlink\")?;\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            stable = %stable.display(),\n            \"rolled back to previous stable\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Check the current release channel status.\n    pub fn status(&self) -> Result<ChannelStatus> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        let testing_exists = testing.exists();\n        let stable_exists = stable.exists();\n        let prev_exists = prev.exists();\n\n        let symlink_target = if symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::read_link(&symlink).ok()\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n\n        Ok(ChannelStatus {\n            testing_exists,\n            stable_exists,\n            prev_exists,\n            symlink_target,\n            testing_path: testing,\n            stable_path: stable,\n            prev_path: prev,\n            symlink_path: symlink,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n// final_status,\n            labels,\n            state_transitions: Vec::new(), // Not tracked in basic canary tests\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Check if actual outcome matches expected outcome.\n    fn outcomes_match(&self, expected: &ExpectedOutcome, actual: &ActualOutcome) -> bool {\n        match expected {\n            ExpectedOutcome::Success {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                actual.final_status == *final_status\n                    && labels.iter().all(|l| actual.labels.contains(l))\n                    && actual.exit_code == Some(0)\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Failure {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                actual.final_status == *final_status\n                    && labels.iter().all(|l| actual.labels.contains(l))\n                    && actual.exit_code.is_some_and(|c| c != 0)\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Timeout { final_status } => {\n                // Timeout is harder to detect from exit code alone.\n                // We check that the bead was not closed (still open/in_progress).\n                actual.final_status == *final_status\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::StateMachine { transitions } => {\n                // Check that all expected transitions occurred.\n                transitions\n                    .iter()\n                    .all(|t| actual.state_transitions.contains(t))\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Generate a human-readable reason for mismatch.\n    fn mismatch_reason(&self, expected: &ExpectedOutcome, actual: &ActualOutcome) -> String {\n        match expected {\n            ExpectedOutcome::Success {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                let mut reasons = Vec::new();\n                if actual.final_status != *final_status {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\n                        \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                        final_status, actual.final_status\n                    ));\n                }\n                for label in labels {\n                    if !actual.labels.contains(label) {\n                        reasons.push(format!(\"missing label: '{}'\", label));\n                    }\n                }\n                if actual.exit_code != Some(0) {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\"expected exit 0, got {:?}\", actual.exit_code));\n                }\n                reasons.join(\"; \")\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Failure {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                let mut reasons = Vec::new();\n                if actual.final_status != *final_status {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\n                        \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                        final_status, actual.final_status\n                    ));\n                }\n                for label in labels {\n                    if !actual.labels.contains(label) {\n                        reasons.push(format!(\"missing label: '{}'\", label));\n                    }\n                }\n                if actual.exit_code == Some(0) {\n                    reasons.push(\"expected non-zero exit, got 0\".to_string());\n                }\n                reasons.join(\"; \")\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Timeout { final_status } => {\n                format!(\n                    \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                    final_status, actual.final_status\n                )\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::StateMachine { transitions } => {\n                let missing: Vec<_> = transitions\n                    .iter()\n                    .filter(|t| !actual.state_transitions.contains(*t))\n                    .collect();\n                format!(\"missing state transitions: {:?}\", missing)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Promote :testing to :stable, backing up the current :stable.\n    ///\n    /// This operation is atomic at the filesystem level:\n    /// 1. Move :stable to :stable.prev\n    /// 2. Move :testing to :stable\n    /// 3. Update symlink\n    pub fn promote(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        if !testing.exists() {\n            bail!(\"testing binary not found: {}\", testing.display());\n        }\n\n        // Ensure bin directory exists.\n        let bin_dir = self.needle_home.join(\"bin\");\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&bin_dir).context(\"failed to create bin directory\")?;\n\n        // Step 1: Remove old backup if exists.\n        if prev.exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&prev).context(\"failed to remove old backup\")?;\n        }\n\n        // Step 2: Move current stable to backup (if exists).\n        if stable.exists() {\n            std::fs::rename(&stable, &prev).context(\"failed to backup stable binary\")?;\n        }\n\n        // Step 3: Move testing to stable.\n        std::fs::rename(&testing, &stable).context(\"failed to promote testing to stable\")?;\n\n        // Step 4: Update symlink.\n        if symlink.exists() || symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&symlink).context(\"failed to remove old symlink\")?;\n        }\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to create symlink\")?;\n        #[cfg(not(unix))]\n        {\n            // Fallback: copy instead of symlink on non-Unix.\n            std::fs::copy(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to copy stable to symlink\")?;\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            testing = %testing.display(),\n            stable = %stable.display(),\n            prev = %prev.display(),\n            symlink = %symlink.display(),\n            \"promoted testing to stable\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Reject :testing (discard without promoting).\n    ///\n    /// The fleet remains on :stable unchanged.\n    pub fn reject(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n\n        if testing.exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&testing).context(\"failed to remove testing binary\")?;\n            tracing::info!(path = %testing.display(), \"rejected testing binary\");\n        } else {\n            tracing::warn!(\"no testing binary to reject\");\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Rollback to the previous stable binary.\n    ///\n    /// Restores :stable.prev as :stable.\n    pub fn rollback(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        if !prev.exists() {\n            bail!(\"no previous stable binary to rollback to\");\n        }\n\n        // Move current stable aside (if exists) - it becomes the new backup.\n        if stable.exists() {\n            // Remove the old backup first since we're about to replace it.\n            let old_backup = self.needle_home.join(\"bin/needle-stable.rollback\");\n            if old_backup.exists() {\n                std::fs::remove_file(&old_backup)?;\n            }\n            std::fs::rename(&stable, &old_backup)?;\n        }\n\n        // Restore previous stable.\n        std::fs::rename(&prev, &stable).context(\"failed to restore previous stable\")?;\n\n        // Update symlink.\n        if symlink.exists() || symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&symlink)?;\n        }\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to update symlink\")?;\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            stable = %stable.display(),\n            \"rolled back to previous stable\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Check the current release channel status.\n    pub fn status(&self) -> Result<ChannelStatus> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        let testing_exists = testing.exists();\n        let stable_exists = stable.exists();\n        let prev_exists = prev.exists();\n\n        let symlink_target = if symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::read_link(&symlink).ok()\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n\n        Ok(ChannelStatus {\n            testing_exists,\n            stable_exists,\n            prev_exists,\n            symlink_target,\n            testing_path: testing,\n            stable_path: stable,\n            prev_path: prev,\n            symlink_path: symlink,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ChannelStatus\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Status of the   final_status: String,\n        /// Expected labels to be present on the bead.\n        #[serde(default)]\n        labels: Vec<String>,\n    },\n    /// Agent should fail (non-zero exit).\n    Failure {\n        /// Expected final bead status.\n        #[serde(default = \"ExpectedOutcome::default_failure_status\")]\n        final_status: String,\n        /// Expected failure labels (e.g., \"failure-count:1\").\n        #[serde(default)]\n        labels: Vec<String>,\n    },\n    /// Agent should timeout.\n    Timeout {\n        /// Expected final bead status.\n        #[serde(default = \"ExpectedOutcome::default_timeout_status\")]\n        final_status: String,\n    },\n    /// Worker state machine should transition correctly.\n    StateMachine {\n        /// Expected state transitions (e.g., [\"BOOTING\", \"SELECTING\", \"CLAIMING\", ...]).\n        transitions: Vec<String>,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl ExpectedOutcome {\n    fn default_final_status() -> String {\n        \"closed\".to_string()\n    }\n    fn default_failure_status() -> String {\n        \"open\".to_string()\n    }\n    fn default_timeout_status() -> String {\n        \"open\".to_string()\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ActualOutcome\n// ────────────────────────────────────────────────��─────────────────────────────\n\n/// Actual outcome observed from running a canary test.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct ActualOutcome {\n    /// Agent exit code (if applicable).\n    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,\n    /// Final bead status.\n    pub final_status: String,\n    /// Labels present on the bead after execution.\n    pub labels: Vec<String>,\n    /// Worker state transitions observed (if tracked).\n    #[serde(default)]\n    pub state_transitions: Vec<String>,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// CanaryReport\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Summary report from running the full canary test suite.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct CanaryReport {\n    /// Path to the testing binary that was tested.\n    pub testing_binary: PathBuf,\n    /// Canary workspace path.\n    pub workspace: PathBuf,\n    /// Total number of tests run.\n    pub total_tests: usize,\n    /// Number of tests that passed.\n    pub passed: usize,\n    /// Number of tests that failed.\n    pub failed: usize,\n    /// Number of tests that timed out.\n    pub timed_out: usize,\n    /// Number of tests that had errors.\n    pub errors: usize,\n    /// Total duration of the canary run.\n    pub duration_secs: u64,\n    /// Individual test results.\n    pub results: Vec<CanaryTestResult>,\n    /// Whether the canary suite passed (all tests passed).\n    pub suite_passed: bool,\n}\n\nimpl CanaryReport {\n    /// Returns true if all tests passed.\n    pub fn can_promote(&self) -> bool {\n        self.suite_passed\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// CanaryRunner\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Runs canary tests against a :testing binary.\npub struct CanaryRunner {\n    /// Path to the needle home directory (~/.needle).\n    needle_home: PathBuf,\n    /// Path to the canary workspace.\n    canary_workspace: PathBuf,\n    /// Timeout for individual tests (seconds).\n    test_timeout: u64,\n}\n\nimpl CanaryRunner {\n    /// Create a new canary runner.\n    pub fn new(needle_home: PathBuf, canary_workspace: PathBuf, test_timeout: u64) -> Self {\n        CanaryRunner {\n            needle_home,\n            canary_workspace,\n            test_timeout,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Path to the testing binary.\n    pub fn testing_binary(&self) -> PathBuf {\n        self.needle_home.join(\"bin/needle-testing\")\n    }\n\n    /// Path to the stable binary.\n    pub fn stable_binary(&self) -> PathBuf {\n        self.needle_home.join(\"bin/needle-stable\")\n    }\n\n    /// Path to the previous stable binary (backup).\n    pub fn prev_binary(&self) -> PathBuf {\n        self.needle_home.join(\"bin/needle-stable.prev\")\n    }\n\n    /// Path to the needle symlink.\n    pub fn symlink_path(&self) -> PathBuf {\n        self.needle_home.join(\"bin/needle\")\n    }\n\n    /// Run the full canary test suite against the :testing binary.\n    ///\n    /// Returns a report with pass/fail status for each test.\n    pub fn run(&self) -> Result<CanaryReport> {\n        let start = Instant::now();\n        let testing_binary = self.testing_binary();\n\n        // Verify testing binary exists.\n        if !testing_binary.exists() {\n            bail!(\"testing binary not found: {}\", testing_binary.display());\n        }\n\n        // Verify canary workspace exists.\n        if !self.canary_workspace.exists() {\n            bail!(\n                \"canary workspace not found: {}\",\n                self.canary_workspace.display()\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Validate canary workspace has authoritative bead_cli.backend binding.\n        // This prevents the canary from inheriting a machine-local legacy binding\n        // that may not exist in production environments (2026-08-15 incident).\n        self.validate_bead_backend_binding()?;\n\n        // Discover test beads in the canary workspace.\n        let test_beads = self.discover_test_beads()?;\n        if test_beads.is_empty() {\n            bail!(\"no test beads found in canary workspace\");\n        }\n\n        let mut results = Vec::new();\n        let mut passed = 0;\n        let mut failed = 0;\n        let mut timed_out = 0;\n        let mut errors = 0;\n\n        for bead_id in &test_beads {\n            // Load expected outcome for this test.\n            let expected = match self.load_expected_outcome(bead_id) {\n                Ok(e) => e,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    results.push(CanaryTestResult::Error {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        message: format!(\"failed to load expected outcome: {e}\"),\n                    });\n                    errors += 1;\n                    continue;\n                }\n            };\n\n            // Run the test.\n            let result = self.run_test(bead_id, &expected, &testing_binary);\n            match &result {\n                CanaryTestResult::Passed { .. } => passed += 1,\n                CanaryTestResult::Failed { .. } => failed += 1,\n                CanaryTestResult::TimedOut { .. } => timed_out += 1,\n                CanaryTestResult::Error { .. } => errors += 1,\n            }\n            results.push(result);\n        }\n\n        let suite_passed = failed == 0 && timed_out == 0 && errors == 0;\n        let total_tests = test_beads.len();\n\n        Ok(CanaryReport {\n            testing_binary,\n            workspace: self.canary_workspace.clone(),\n            total_tests,\n            passed,\n            failed,\n            timed_out,\n            errors,\n            duration_secs: start.elapsed().as_secs(),\n            results,\n            suite_passed,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Validate that the canary workspace has an authoritative bead_cli.backend binding.\n    ///\n    /// This prevents environmental failures where the canary workspace inherits\n    /// a machine-local legacy binding that may not exist in production.\n    fn validate_bead_backend_binding(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let workspace_config = crate::config::ConfigLoader::load_workspace(&self.canary_workspace)\n            .with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"failed to load .needle.yaml for canary workspace {}\",\n                    self.canary_workspace.display()\n                )\n            })?;\n\n        // Both a missing `.needle.yaml` (`load_workspace` yields `None`) and a\n        // missing `bead_cli` section leave the canary on the same implicit\n        // `auto` binding as an explicit one, so all three are rejected here.\n        let bead_cli = match workspace_config\n            .as_ref()\n            .and_then(|overrides| overrides.bead_cli.as_ref())\n        {\n            Some(cli) if !matches!(cli.backend, crate::config::BeadBackend::Auto) => cli,\n            _ => bail!(\n                \"canary workspace {} has no authoritative bead_cli.backend binding (currently set to 'auto'). \\\n                 This causes environmental failures when the canary inherits a machine-local legacy binding. \\\n                 Fix by adding to {}/.needle.yaml:\\n  bead_cli:\\n    backend: bead-rs\\nor\\n    backend: bead-forge\",\n                self.canary_workspace.display(),\n                self.canary_workspace.display()\n            ),\n        };\n        let backend = &bead_cli.backend;\n\n        // Verify the backend binary exists\n        let (backend_type, binary_path) =\n            crate::config::resolve_bead_cli(bead_cli).with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"failed to resolve bead CLI backend '{}' for canary workspace {}\",\n                    backend,\n                    self.canary_workspace.display()\n                )\n            })?;\n\n        if !binary_path.exists() {\n            bail!(\n                \"bead CLI backend '{}' binary not found: {} (backend: {})\\n\\\n                 Ensure the backend is installed and accessible, or update bead_cli.path in {}/.needle.yaml\",\n                backend,\n                binary_path.display(),\n                backend_type,\n                self.canary_workspace.display()\n            );\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            backend = %backend,\n            binary = %binary_path.display(),\n            resolved_backend = %backend_type,\n            \"canary workspace bead backend validated\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Discover test bead IDs in the canary workspace.\n    fn discover_test_beads(&self) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n        let expected_dir = self.canary_workspace.join(\"expected\");\n        if !expected_dir.exists() {\n            bail!(\n                \"expected outcomes directory not found: {}\",\n                expected_dir.display()\n            );\n        }\n\n        let mut bead_ids = Vec::new();\n        for entry in std::fs::read_dir(&expected_dir)? {\n            let entry = entry?;\n            let path = entry.path();\n            if path.extension().is_some_and(|e| e == \"yaml\") {\n                if let Some(stem) = path.file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) {\n                    bead_ids.push(stem.to_string());\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(bead_ids)\n    }\n\n    /// Load the expected outcome for a test bead.\n    fn load_expected_outcome(&self, bead_id: &str) -> Result<ExpectedOutcome> {\n        let path = self\n            .canary_workspace\n            .join(\"expected\")\n            .join(format!(\"{bead_id}.yaml\"));\n        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read expected outcome: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        serde_yaml::from_str(&content)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid expected outcome YAML: {}\", path.display()))\n    }\n\n    /// Run a single canary test.\n    ///\n    /// Spawns the testing binary and polls for completion, killing the process\n    /// and returning [`CanaryTestResult::TimedOut`] if it exceeds `test_timeout`.\n    fn run_test(\n        &self,\n        bead_id: &str,\n        expected: &ExpectedOutcome,\n        testing_binary: &Path,\n    ) -> CanaryTestResult {\n        let start = Instant::now();\n        let timeout = Duration::from_secs(self.test_timeout);\n\n        // Spawn the testing binary against the canary workspace.\n        //\n        // `--workspace` alone does NOT confine the worker. The Explore strand is\n        // enabled by default and, with `workspaces` empty, scans\n        // `workspace_root` — which defaults to $HOME — for every bead workspace\n        // on the box. A canary worker spawned without isolation therefore roams\n        // into the operator's real repos and dispatches agents against them: on\n        // 2026-08-07 a single `needle upgrade` put four agents into spaxel and\n        // bead-forge, where they ran git commands and left files behind. This is\n        // the same escape ADR-006 documents for tests, and the isolation policy\n        // in CLAUDE.md was never applied to the canary runner itself.\n        //\n        // Pin the scan root to the canary workspace and switch Explore off, so a\n        // canary run can only ever touch beads that live in the canary.\n        //\n        // CRITICAL: Set NEEDLE_INNER=1 to prevent the worker from detaching into\n        // tmux. Without this, the worker runs in the background and the canary\n        // evaluates outcomes before work finishes, producing false negatives.\n        //\n        // CRITICAL: Isolate HOME to prevent reading global config at\n        // ~/.config/needle/config.yaml or ~/.needle/. This ensures the canary\n        // worker only reads from the canary workspace's .needle.yaml.\n        //\n        // CRITICAL: Use explicit adapter selection (echo) to avoid inheriting\n        // obsolete adapter names from global config (e.g., 'opus' which was\n        // deprecated in favor of 'claude-anthropic-opus'). The echo adapter is\n        // hermetic and always available for testing.\n        //\n        // Use retry wrapper to handle ETXTBSY (errno 26) which can occur when\n        // spawning a testing binary that was written to disk immediately before\n        // execution (race condition between write close and kernel page cache sync).\n        let mut child = match crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential_child(\n            || {\n                Command::new(testing_binary)\n                    .args([\n                        \"run\",\n                        \"--workspace\",\n                        &self.canary_workspace.display().to_string(),\n                        \"--agent\",\n                        \"echo\", // Use explicit hermetic adapter, not global default\n                        \"--identifier\",\n                        &format!(\"canary-{bead_id}\"),\n                        \"--count\",\n                        \"1\",\n                    ])\n                    .env(\"NEEDLE_INNER\", \"1\")\n                    .env(\"NEEDLE_STRANDS__EXPLORE__ENABLED\", \"false\")\n                    .env(\n                        \"NEEDLE_STRANDS__EXPLORE__WORKSPACE_ROOT\",\n                        &self.canary_workspace,\n                    )\n                    .env(\"HOME\", &self.canary_workspace)\n                    .spawn()\n            },\n            10,\n            20,\n        ) {\n            Ok(c) => c,\n            Err(e) => {\n                return CanaryTestResult::Error {\n                    bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                    message: format!(\"failed to spawn testing binary: {e}\"),\n                };\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Poll for completion, enforcing the timeout.\n        let exit_code = loop {\n            match child.try_wait() {\n                Ok(Some(status)) => break status.code(),\n                Ok(None) => {\n                    if start.elapsed() >= timeout {\n                        child.kill().ok();\n                        return CanaryTestResult::TimedOut {\n                            bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                            elapsed_secs: start.elapsed().as_secs(),\n                        };\n                    }\n                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500));\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    return CanaryTestResult::Error {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                        message: format!(\"failed to wait for testing binary: {e}\"),\n                    };\n                }\n            }\n        };\n\n        let actual = match self.get_actual_outcome(bead_id, exit_code) {\n            Ok(a) => a,\n            Err(e) => {\n                return CanaryTestResult::Error {\n                    bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                    message: format!(\"failed to get actual outcome: {e}\"),\n                };\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Compare actual vs expected.\n        if self.outcomes_match(expected, &actual) {\n            CanaryTestResult::Passed {\n                bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                expected: expected.clone(),\n                actual,\n            }\n        } else {\n            let reason = self.mismatch_reason(expected, &actual);\n            CanaryTestResult::Failed {\n                bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                expected: expected.clone(),\n                actual,\n                reason,\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get the actual outcome for a test bead by querying the bead store.\n    fn get_actual_outcome(&self, bead_id: &str, exit_code: Option<i32>) -> Result<ActualOutcome> {\n        let workspace_config = crate::config::ConfigLoader::load_workspace(&self.canary_workspace)?\n            .with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"canary workspace {} has no .needle.yaml\",\n                    self.canary_workspace.display()\n                )\n            })?;\n        let bead_cli = workspace_config.bead_cli.with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"canary workspace {} has no authoritative bead_cli.backend binding\",\n                self.canary_workspace.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n        let (_, binary) = crate::config::resolve_bead_cli(&bead_cli).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to resolve canary workspace bead backend '{}'\",\n                bead_cli.backend\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        let output = crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync(\n            || {\n                Command::new(&binary)\n                    .args([\"show\", bead_id, \"--json\"])\n                    .current_dir(&self.canary_workspace)\n                    .output()\n            },\n            5,\n            20,\n        )\n        .with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to run {} show for backend '{}'\",\n                binary.display(),\n                bead_cli.backend\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        if !output.status.success() {\n            bail!(\n                \"backend '{}' show failed for bead {}: {}\",\n                bead_cli.backend,\n                bead_id,\n                String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim()\n            );\n        }\n\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n        let projection: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&stdout)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to parse '{}' show output\", bead_cli.backend))?;\n        // bead-rs returns a one-element array; bead-forge returns an object.\n        let bead = projection\n            .as_array()\n            .and_then(|items| items.first())\n            .unwrap_or(&projection);\n\n        let final_status = bead[\"status\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"unknown\").to_string();\n        let labels = bead[\"labels\"]\n            .as_array()\n            .map(|arr| {\n                arr.iter()\n                    .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(|s| s.to_string()))\n                    .collect()\n            })\n            .unwrap_or_default();\n\n        Ok(ActualOutcome {\n            exit_code,\n            final_status,\n            labels,\n            state_transitions: Vec::new(), // Not tracked in basic canary tests\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Check if actual outcome matches expected outcome.\n    fn outcomes_match(&self, expected: &ExpectedOutcome, actual: &ActualOutcome) -> bool {\n        match expected {\n            ExpectedOutcome::Success {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                actual.final_status == *final_status\n                    && labels.iter().all(|l| actual.labels.contains(l))\n                    && actual.exit_code == Some(0)\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Failure {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                actual.final_status == *final_status\n                    && labels.iter().all(|l| actual.labels.contains(l))\n                    && actual.exit_code.is_some_and(|c| c != 0)\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Timeout { final_status } => {\n                // Timeout is harder to detect from exit code alone.\n                // We check that the bead was not closed (still open/in_progress).\n                actual.final_status == *final_status\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::StateMachine { transitions } => {\n                // Check that all expected transitions occurred.\n                transitions\n                    .iter()\n                    .all(|t| actual.state_transitions.contains(t))\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Generate a human-readable reason for mismatch.\n    fn mismatch_reason(&self, expected: &ExpectedOutcome, actual: &ActualOutcome) -> String {\n        match expected {\n            ExpectedOutcome::Success {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                let mut reasons = Vec::new();\n                if actual.final_status != *final_status {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\n                        \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                        final_status, actual.final_status\n                    ));\n                }\n                for label in labels {\n                    if !actual.labels.contains(label) {\n                        reasons.push(format!(\"missing label: '{}'\", label));\n                    }\n                }\n                if actual.exit_code != Some(0) {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\"expected exit 0, got {:?}\", actual.exit_code));\n                }\n                reasons.join(\"; \")\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Failure {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                let mut reasons = Vec::new();\n                if actual.final_status != *final_status {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\n                        \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                        final_status, actual.final_status\n                    ));\n                }\n                for label in labels {\n                    if !actual.labels.contains(label) {\n                        reasons.push(format!(\"missing label: '{}'\", label));\n                    }\n                }\n                if actual.exit_code == Some(0) {\n                    reasons.push(\"expected non-zero exit, got 0\".to_string());\n                }\n                reasons.join(\"; \")\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Timeout { final_status } => {\n                format!(\n                    \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                    final_status, actual.final_status\n                )\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::StateMachine { transitions } => {\n                let missing: Vec<_> = transitions\n                    .iter()\n                    .filter(|t| !actual.state_transitions.contains(*t))\n                    .collect();\n                format!(\"missing state transitions: {:?}\", missing)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Promote :testing to :stable, backing up the current :stable.\n    ///\n    /// This operation is atomic at the filesystem level:\n    /// 1. Move :stable to :stable.prev\n    /// 2. Move :testing to :stable\n    /// 3. Update symlink\n    pub fn promote(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        if !testing.exists() {\n            bail!(\"testing binary not found: {}\", testing.display());\n        }\n\n        // Ensure bin directory exists.\n        let bin_dir = self.needle_home.join(\"bin\");\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&bin_dir).context(\"failed to create bin directory\")?;\n\n        // Step 1: Remove old backup if exists.\n        if prev.exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&prev).context(\"failed to remove old backup\")?;\n        }\n\n        // Step 2: Move current stable to backup (if exists).\n        if stable.exists() {\n            std::fs::rename(&stable, &prev).context(\"failed to backup stable binary\")?;\n        }\n\n        // Step 3: Move testing to stable.\n        std::fs::rename(&testing, &stable).context(\"failed to promote testing to stable\")?;\n\n        // Step 4: Update symlink.\n        if symlink.exists() || symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&symlink).context(\"failed to remove old symlink\")?;\n        }\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to create symlink\")?;\n        #[cfg(not(unix))]\n        {\n            // Fallback: copy instead of symlink on non-Unix.\n            std::fs::copy(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to copy stable to symlink\")?;\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            testing = %testing.display(),\n            stable = %stable.display(),\n            prev = %prev.display(),\n            symlink = %symlink.display(),\n            \"promoted testing to stable\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Reject :testing (discard without promoting).\n    ///\n    /// The fleet remains on :stable unchanged.\n    pub fn reject(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n\n        if testing.exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&testing).context(\"failed to remove testing binary\")?;\n            tracing::info!(path = %testing.display(), \"rejected testing binary\");\n        } else {\n            tracing::warn!(\"no testing binary to reject\");\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Rollback to the previous stable binary.\n    ///\n    /// Restores :stable.prev as :stable.\n    pub fn rollback(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        if !prev.exists() {\n            bail!(\"no previous stable binary to rollback to\");\n        }\n\n        // Move current stable aside (if exists) - it becomes the new backup.\n        if stable.exists() {\n            // Remove the old backup first since we're about to replace it.\n            let old_backup = self.needle_home.join(\"bin/needle-stable.rollback\");\n            if old_backup.exists() {\n                std::fs::remove_file(&old_backup)?;\n            }\n            std::fs::rename(&stable, &old_backup)?;\n        }\n\n        // Restore previous stable.\n        std::fs::rename(&prev, &stable).context(\"failed to restore previous stable\")?;\n\n        // Update symlink.\n        if symlink.exists() || symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&symlink)?;\n        }\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to update symlink\")?;\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            stable = %stable.display(),\n            \"rolled back to previous stable\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Check the current release channel status.\n    pub fn status(&self) -> Result<ChannelStatus> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        let testing_exists = testing.exists();\n        let stable_exists = stable.exists();\n        let prev_exists = prev.exists();\n\n        let symlink_target = if symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::read_link(&symlink).ok()\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n\n        Ok(ChannelStatus {\n            testing_exists,\n            stable_exists,\n            prev_exists,\n            symlink_target,\n            testing_path: testing,\n            stable_path: stable,\n            prev_path: prev,\n            symlink_path: symlink,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n// actual_outcome_uses_workspace_backend_and_accepts_both_show_shapes() {\n        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;\n\n        for (backend, projection) in [\n            (\"bead-rs\", r#\"[{\"status\":\"closed\",\"labels\":[\"native\"]}]\"#),\n            (\"bead-forge\", r#\"{\"status\":\"open\",\"labels\":[\"forge\"]}\"#),\n        ] {\n            let root = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();\n            let binary = root.path().join(\"bound-backend\");\n            std::fs::write(\n                &binary,\n                format!(\"#!/bin/sh\\nprintf '%s\\\\n' '{projection}'\\n\"),\n            )\n            .unwrap();\n            let mut permissions = std::fs::metadata(&binary).unwrap().permissions();\n            permissions.set_mode(0o755);\n            std::fs::set_permissions(&binary, permissions).unwrap();\n            std::fs::write(\n                root.path().join(\".needle.yaml\"),\n                format!(\n                    \"bead_cli:\\n  backend: {backend}\\n  path: {}\\n\",\n                    binary.display()\n                ),\n            )\n            .unwrap();\n\n            let runner = CanaryRunner::new(root.path().join(\"needle\"), root.path().into(), 30);\n            let actual = runner.get_actual_outcome(\"example-1\", Some(0)).unwrap();\n            if backend == \"bead-rs\" {\n                assert_eq!(actual.final_status, \"closed\");\n                assert_eq!(actual.labels, vec![\"native\"]);\n            } else {\n                assert_eq!(actual.final_status, \"open\");\n                assert_eq!(actual.labels, vec![\"forge\"]);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn canary_test_result_is_pass() {\n        let passed = },\n}\n\nimpl CanaryTestResult {\n    /// Returns true if this result represents a pass.\n    pub fn is_pass(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, CanaryTestResult::Passed { .. })\n    }\n\n    /// CanaryTestResult::Error { .. } => errors += 1,\n            }\n            results.push(result);\n        }\n\n        let suite_passed = failed == 0 && timed_out == 0 && errors == 0;\n        let self.canary_workspace.display(),\n                self.canary_workspace.display()\n            ),\n        };\n        let backend = &bead_cli.backend;\n\n        // Verify the backend binary exists\n        let (backend_type, binary_path) =\n            crate::config::resolve_bead_cli(bead_cli).with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"failed to resolve bead CLI backend '{}' for canary workspace {}\",\n                    backend,\n                    self.canary_workspace.display()\n                )\n            })?;\n\n        if !binary_path.exists() {\n   tracing::info!(\n            backend = %backend,\n            binary = %binary_path.display(),\n            resolved_backend = %backend_type,\n            \"canary workspace bead backend expected_dir.display()\n            );\n        }\n\n        let mut bead_ids = Vec::new();\n        for entry in std::fs::read_dir(&expected_dir)? {\n            let entry = entry?;\n            let path = entry.path();\n            if path.extension().is_some_and(|e| e == \"yaml\") {\n                if let Some(stem) = path.file_stem().and_then(|s| s.to_str()) {\n                    bead_ids.push(stem.to_string());\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(bead_ids)\n    }\n\n    /// Load the expected outcome for a test bead.\n    fn load_expected_outcome(&self, bead_id: &str) -> Result<ExpectedOutcome> {\n        let path = self\n            .canary_workspace\n            .join(\"expected\")\n            .join(format!(\"{bead_id}.yaml\"));\n        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to read expected outcome: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        serde_yaml::from_str(&content)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid expected outcome YAML: {}\", path.display()))\n    }\n\n    /// Run a single canary test.\n    ///\n    /// Spawns the testing binary and polls for completion, killing the process\n    /// and returning [`CanaryTestResult::TimedOut`] if it exceeds `test_timeout`.\n    fn run_test(\n        &self,\n        bead_id: &str,\n        expected: &ExpectedOutcome,\n        testing_binary: &Path,\n    ) -> CanaryTestResult {\n        let start = Instant::now();\n        let timeout = Duration::from_secs(self.test_timeout);\n\n        // Spawn the testing binary against the canary workspace.\n        //\n        // `--workspace` alone does NOT confine the worker. The Explore strand is\n        // enabled by default and, with `workspaces` empty, scans\n        // `workspace_root` — which defaults to $HOME — for every bead workspace\n        // on the box. A canary worker spawned without isolation therefore roams\n        // into the operator's real repos and dispatches agents against them: on\n        // 2026-08-07 a single `needle upgrade` put four agents into spaxel and\n        // bead-forge, where they ran git commands and left files behind. This is\n        // the same escape ADR-006 documents for tests, and the isolation policy\n        // in CLAUDE.md was never applied to the canary runner itself.\n        //\n        // Pin the scan root to the canary workspace and switch Explore off, so a\n        // canary run can only ever touch beads that live in the canary.\n        //\n        // CRITICAL: Set NEEDLE_INNER=1 to prevent the worker from detaching into\n        // tmux. Without this, the worker runs in the background and the canary\n        // evaluates outcomes before work finishes, producing false negatives.\n        //\n        // CRITICAL: Isolate HOME to prevent reading global config at\n        // ~/.config/needle/config.yaml or ~/.needle/. This ensures the canary\n        // worker only reads from the canary workspace's .needle.yaml.\n        //\n        // CRITICAL: Use explicit adapter selection (echo) to avoid inheriting\n        // obsolete adapter names from global config (e.g., 'opus' which was\n        // deprecated in favor of 'claude-anthropic-opus'). The echo adapter is\n        // hermetic and always available for testing.\n        //\n        // Use retry wrapper to handle ETXTBSY (errno 26) which can occur when\n        // spawning a testing binary that was written to disk immediately before\n        // execution (race condition between write close and kernel page cache sync).\n        let mut child = match crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential_child(\n            || {\n                Command::new(testing_binary)\n                    .args([\n                        \"run\",\n                        \"--workspace\",\n                        &self.canary_workspace.display().to_string(),\n                        \"--agent\",\n                        \"echo\", // Use explicit hermetic adapter, not global default\n                        \"--identifier\",\n                        &format!(\"canary-{bead_id}\"),\n                        \"--count\",\n                        \"1\",\n                    ])\n                    .env(\"NEEDLE_INNER\", \"1\")\n                    .env(\"NEEDLE_STRANDS__EXPLORE__ENABLED\", \"false\")\n                    .env(\n                        \"NEEDLE_STRANDS__EXPLORE__WORKSPACE_ROOT\",\n                        &self.canary_workspace,\n                    )\n                    .env(\"HOME\", &self.canary_workspace)\n                    .spawn()\n            },\n            10,\n            20,\n        ) {\n            Ok(c) => c,\n            Err(e) => {\n                return CanaryTestResult::Error {\n                    bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                    message: format!(\"failed to spawn testing binary: {e}\"),\n                };\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Poll for completion, enforcing the timeout.\n        let exit_code = loop {\n            match child.try_wait() {\n                Ok(Some(status)) => break status.code(),\n                Ok(None) => {\n                    if start.elapsed() >= timeout {\n                        child.kill().ok();\n                        return CanaryTestResult::TimedOut {\n                            bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                            elapsed_secs: start.elapsed().as_secs(),\n                        };\n                    }\n                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500));\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    return CanaryTestResult::Error {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                        message: format!(\"failed to wait for testing binary: {e}\"),\n                    };\n                }\n            }\n        };\n\n        let actual = match self.get_actual_outcome(bead_id, exit_code) {\n            Ok(a) => a,\n            Err(e) => {\n                return CanaryTestResult::Error {\n                    bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                    message: format!(\"failed to get actual outcome: {e}\"),\n                };\n            }\n        };\n\n        // Compare actual vs expected.\n        if self.outcomes_match(expected, &actual) {\n            CanaryTestResult::Passed {\n                bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                expected: expected.clone(),\n                actual,\n            }\n        } else {\n            let reason = self.mismatch_reason(expected, &actual);\n            CanaryTestResult::Failed {\n                bead_id: bead_id.to_string(),\n                expected: expected.clone(),\n                actual,\n                reason,\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get the actual outcome for a test bead by querying the bead store.\n    fn get_actual_outcome(&self, bead_id: &str, exit_code: Option<i32>) -> Result<ActualOutcome> {\n        let workspace_config = crate::config::ConfigLoader::load_workspace(&self.canary_workspace)?\n            .with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"canary workspace {} has no .needle.yaml\",\n                    self.canary_workspace.display()\n                )\n            })?;\n        let bead_cli = workspace_config.bead_cli.with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"canary workspace {} has no authoritative bead_cli.backend binding\",\n                self.canary_workspace.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n        let (_, binary) = crate::config::resolve_bead_cli(&bead_cli).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to resolve canary workspace bead backend '{}'\",\n                bead_cli.backend\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        let output = crate::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync(\n            || {\n                Command::new(&binary)\n                    .args([\"show\", bead_id, \"--json\"])\n                    .current_dir(&self.canary_workspace)\n                    .output()\n            },\n            5,\n            20,\n        )\n        .with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to run {} show for backend '{}'\",\n                binary.display(),\n                bead_cli.backend\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        if !output.status.success() {\n            bail!(\n                \"backend '{}' show failed for bead {}: {}\",\n                bead_cli.backend,\n                bead_id,\n                String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim()\n            );\n        }\n\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n        let projection: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&stdout)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to parse '{}' show output\", bead_cli.backend))?;\n        // bead-rs returns a one-element array; bead-forge returns an object.\n        let bead = projection\n            .as_array()\n            .and_then(|items| items.first())\n            .unwrap_or(&projection);\n\n        let final_status = bead[\"status\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"unknown\").to_string();\n        let labels = bead[\"labels\"]\n            .as_array()\n            .map(|arr| {\n                arr.iter()\n                    .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(|s| s.to_string()))\n                    .collect()\n            })\n            .unwrap_or_default();\n\n        Ok(ActualOutcome {\n            exit_code,\n            final_status,\n            labels,\n            state_transitions: Vec::new(), // Not tracked in basic canary tests\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Check if actual outcome matches expected outcome.\n    fn outcomes_match(&self, expected: &ExpectedOutcome, actual: &ActualOutcome) -> bool {\n        match expected {\n            ExpectedOutcome::Success {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                actual.final_status == *final_status\n                    && labels.iter().all(|l| actual.labels.contains(l))\n                    && actual.exit_code == Some(0)\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Failure {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                actual.final_status == *final_status\n                    && labels.iter().all(|l| actual.labels.contains(l))\n                    && actual.exit_code.is_some_and(|c| c != 0)\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Timeout { final_status } => {\n                // Timeout is harder to detect from exit code alone.\n                // We check that the bead was not closed (still open/in_progress).\n                actual.final_status == *final_status\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::StateMachine { transitions } => {\n                // Check that all expected transitions occurred.\n                transitions\n                    .iter()\n                    .all(|t| actual.state_transitions.contains(t))\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Generate a human-readable reason for mismatch.\n    fn mismatch_reason(&self, expected: &ExpectedOutcome, actual: &ActualOutcome) -> String {\n        match expected {\n            ExpectedOutcome::Success {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                let mut reasons = Vec::new();\n                if actual.final_status != *final_status {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\n                        \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                        final_status, actual.final_status\n                    ));\n                }\n                for label in labels {\n                    if !actual.labels.contains(label) {\n                        reasons.push(format!(\"missing label: '{}'\", label));\n                    }\n                }\n                if actual.exit_code != Some(0) {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\"expected exit 0, got {:?}\", actual.exit_code));\n                }\n                reasons.join(\"; \")\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Failure {\n                final_status,\n                labels,\n            } => {\n                let mut reasons = Vec::new();\n                if actual.final_status != *final_status {\n                    reasons.push(format!(\n                        \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                        final_status, actual.final_status\n                    ));\n                }\n                for label in labels {\n                    if !actual.labels.contains(label) {\n                        reasons.push(format!(\"missing label: '{}'\", label));\n                    }\n                }\n                if actual.exit_code == Some(0) {\n                    reasons.push(\"expected non-zero exit, got 0\".to_string());\n                }\n                reasons.join(\"; \")\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::Timeout { final_status } => {\n                format!(\n                    \"status mismatch: expected '{}', got '{}'\",\n                    final_status, actual.final_status\n                )\n            }\n            ExpectedOutcome::StateMachine { transitions } => {\n                let missing: Vec<_> = transitions\n                    .iter()\n                    .filter(|t| !actual.state_transitions.contains(*t))\n                    .collect();\n                format!(\"missing state transitions: {:?}\", missing)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Promote :testing to :stable, backing up the current :stable.\n    ///\n    /// This operation is atomic at the filesystem level:\n    /// 1. Move :stable to :stable.prev\n    /// 2. Move :testing to :stable\n    /// 3. Update symlink\n    pub fn promote(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        if !testing.exists() {\n            bail!(\"testing binary not found: {}\", testing.display());\n        }\n\n        // Ensure bin directory exists.\n        let bin_dir = self.needle_home.join(\"bin\");\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&bin_dir).context(\"failed to create bin directory\")?;\n\n        // Step 1: Remove old backup if exists.\n        if prev.exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&prev).context(\"failed to remove old backup\")?;\n        }\n\n        // Step 2: Move current stable to backup (if exists).\n        if stable.exists() {\n            std::fs::rename(&stable, &prev).context(\"failed to backup stable binary\")?;\n        }\n\n        // Step 3: Move testing to stable.\n        std::fs::rename(&testing, &stable).context(\"failed to promote testing to stable\")?;\n\n        // Step 4: Update symlink.\n        if symlink.exists() || symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&symlink).context(\"failed to remove old symlink\")?;\n        }\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to create symlink\")?;\n        #[cfg(not(unix))]\n        {\n            // Fallback: copy instead of symlink on non-Unix.\n            std::fs::copy(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to copy stable to symlink\")?;\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            testing = %testing.display(),\n            stable = %stable.display(),\n            prev = %prev.display(),\n            symlink = %symlink.display(),\n            \"promoted testing to stable\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Reject :testing (discard without promoting).\n    ///\n    /// The fleet remains on :stable unchanged.\n    pub fn reject(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n\n        if testing.exists() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&testing).context(\"failed to remove testing binary\")?;\n            tracing::info!(path = %testing.display(), \"rejected testing binary\");\n        } else {\n            tracing::warn!(\"no testing binary to reject\");\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Rollback to the previous stable binary.\n    ///\n    /// Restores :stable.prev as :stable.\n    pub fn rollback(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        if !prev.exists() {\n            bail!(\"no previous stable binary to rollback to\");\n        }\n\n        // Move current stable aside (if exists) - it becomes the new backup.\n        if stable.exists() {\n            // Remove the old backup first since we're about to replace it.\n            let old_backup = self.needle_home.join(\"bin/needle-stable.rollback\");\n            if old_backup.exists() {\n                std::fs::remove_file(&old_backup)?;\n            }\n            std::fs::rename(&stable, &old_backup)?;\n        }\n\n        // Restore previous stable.\n        std::fs::rename(&prev, &stable).context(\"failed to restore previous stable\")?;\n\n        // Update symlink.\n        if symlink.exists() || symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::remove_file(&symlink)?;\n        }\n        #[cfg(unix)]\n        std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&stable, &symlink).context(\"failed to update symlink\")?;\n\n        tracing::info!(\n            stable = %stable.display(),\n            \"rolled back to previous stable\"\n        );\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Check the current release channel status.\n    pub fn status(&self) -> Result<ChannelStatus> {\n        let testing = self.testing_binary();\n        let stable = self.stable_binary();\n        let prev = self.prev_binary();\n        let symlink = self.symlink_path();\n\n        let testing_exists = testing.exists();\n        let stable_exists = stable.exists();\n        let prev_exists = prev.exists();\n\n        let symlink_target = if symlink.is_symlink() {\n            std::fs::read_link(&symlink).ok()\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n\n        Ok(ChannelStatus {\n            testing_exists,\n            stable_exists,\n            prev_exists,\n            symlink_target,\n            testing_path: testing,\n            stable_path: stable,\n            prev_path: prev,\n            symlink_path: symlink,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n// release channels.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct ChannelStatus {\n    /// Whether :testing binary exists.\n    pub testing_exists: bool,\n    /// Whether :stable binary exists.\n    pub
